hpi: {{patient_name}} is a child presenting with abdominal pain, constipation, irritability, lethargy, ataxia, and cognitive changes. History reveals exposure to lead-based paint in older home (built <1978). Lead intoxication causes microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling on peripheral smear. Elevated free erythrocyte protoporphyrin (FEP). Definitive diagnosis: blood lead level (BLL) >5 mcg/dL is elevated. >45 mcg/dL requires chelation. >70 mcg/dL is a medical emergency. Chronic lead exposure affects: nervous system (encephalopathy, developmental delay), kidneys (Fanconi syndrome), bone marrow (anemia), GI (colic). Treatment: remove source (lead abatement). Chelation therapy: succimer (DMSA) PO for BLL >45, or IV edetate calcium disodium (EDTA) + dimercaprol (BAL) for lead encephalopathy (BLL >70). Iron supplementation for anemia. Report to public health.
